scenarios.title: Withdraw an obsolete NFS export
scenarios.summary: Remove an obsolete share from the server’s current export list while preserving the archive mount and approved reference access.
scenarios.objective: Save a revised export file that removes the old-bundle share. Keep both remaining export rules unchanged and re-export without disturbing the archive mount. Confirm a fresh retired client cannot mount the old share. The approved client should mount the reference share and read its supplied file. Keep the contents of all the existing files intact.

guide.title: Understand the task
guide.why: The virtual /etc/exports file holds saved settings. Saving an edit does not publish it. On the server, exportfs -v reports which paths and access options are applied now.
guide.action: Inspect and verify the supplied virtual exports.

guide.title: Try the separate example
guide.why: Use exportfs -r or exportfs -ra to publish the saved settings in this exercise. This simulator refuses to change an export when a conflicting current mount depends on it. Unmount only the retired client. Preserve independent working shares.
guide.action: Inspect and verify the supplied virtual exports.

guide.title: Complete the independent assignment
guide.why: showmount -e with the server address shows what the supplied NFSv3 server advertises. A client must still mount the right path and have permission to read its file. Try a fresh mount for the retired client as well.
guide.action: Inspect and verify the supplied virtual exports.

scenarios.retry_guidance: Compare the saved text, applied export list and current client mount before checking again.
hints: Check whether the retired client is still mounted before publishing the isolated change.
Save updates the file. Re-export updates the current list. Test again after doing both.
Verify the approved file independently of the advertised list.
scenarios.explanation: The retired path has been removed from the live list and cannot be mounted again by the retired client. The existing archive and read access to the reference share are both preserved.
scenarios.simplifications: Virtual literal exportfs -v, -r/-ra and showmount -e for the supplied NFSv3 fixture only. The active-mount refusal is a simulator rule, not Linux exportfs rollback. No host command, kernel, RPC, actual host files, V4, netgroups or mountd administration.
